caption: The drawing depicts a single garment, specifically a white apron with a waistband, shown against a plain, light-colored background. The apron features an intricate pattern of eyelet embroidery, forming a decorative triangular or V-shaped design that covers much of the lower front portion of the apron. The embroidery consists of small, evenly spaced circular cut-outs arranged in repetitive, symmetrical motifs that resemble floral and curved, wave-like elements. The hem of the apron is finished with a scalloped edge, which is also highlighted with small embroidered details. The overall color of the apron is a soft white or pale ivory, with light blue or gray shading used to suggest folds, shadows, and the translucency of the fabric. The waistband is plain and undecorated, and the full shape of the apron suggests it is meant to be worn over other clothing. The artist's signature, "Edith Turner," appears in the bottom right corner of the image.
title: Petticoat
